name: NY-24
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+11 partisan lean favors Tenney
No polling and no expert ratings; markets price ~93% Republican
Ellman's minimal cash on hand limits competitiveness
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Tenney's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and Polymarket pricing near 93% Republican all point to a comfortable Tenney win, with no evidence of Democratic strength to justify moving closer.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a tighter race or a surge of Democratic outside spending would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Claudia Tenney seeks another term in a central New York district that leans Republican by about eleven points. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $2.8 million and holding more than $1.3 million on hand, while Democrat Alissa Ellman has raised under $200,000 with little cash remaining.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Tenney around 93 percent. The district's lean, incumbency, and money gap make her the clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
